The story uses original metaphors to deepen its emotional meaning: the fleeing congregation becomes “a river running the wrong way,” making Barbara’s attempt to help the shooter both physically and morally countercurrent. The child crying “Daddy” as though “the word were a handhold” turns language into a desperate source of security. The allusion to the twenty-third Psalm brings communal consolation into tension with the violence, while the beautiful, indifferent amber light underscores the rupture between ordinary surroundings and human catastrophe.
